extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from XML methods/results/discussion and figure captions; direct mechanism is limited to membrane permeability/integrity and microscopy assays.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: BSN-37 increases outer membrane permeability of ST in direct NPN uptake assays, but with weaker fluorescence response than pexiganan.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: BSN-37 against source-defined ST / S. Typhimurium CVCC541

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=19:Effect of BSN-37 on the Cell Membrane of ST;xml:fig=3:FIGURE 3

mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports outer-membrane permeabilization, not generalized membrane lysis or pore formation by itself.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: BSN-37 did not materially impair ST inner membrane integrity in DiS-C3-(5) and beta-galactosidase release assays, supporting a non-lytic mode at tested concentrations.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: BSN-37 against source-defined ST / S. Typhimurium CVCC541

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=19:Effect of BSN-37 on the Cell Membrane of ST;xml:fig=3:FIGURE 3

mechanism_claims.limitations: A small DiS-C3-(5) fluorescence increase is described, so the conclusion is bounded to little/no inner-membrane impairment rather than no membrane effect at all.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM and TEM observations did not show broken or ruptured ST cells after BSN-37 treatment, while pexiganan caused membrane-damage morphology; this supports non-lytic antibacterial action.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: BSN-37 against source-defined ST / S. Typhimurium CVCC541
mechanism_claims.limitations: Microscopy supports absence of gross lysis under tested conditions; it does not identify the intracellular molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper discusses cytoplasmic/intracellular target possibilities for proline-rich Bac5/Bac7 peptides, including ribosomal peptide-exit-tunnel binding by related fragments, but does not directly assay BSN-37 binding to ribosomes or other cytoplasmic targets.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Do not promote protein-synthesis/ribosome inhibition to direct BSN-37 mechanism in this paper.

unrecoverable_material_gaps.why_unrecoverable: The local primary article discusses cytoplasmic targets by analogy to Bac5/Bac7 literature but does not report a BSN-37 ribosome/protein-synthesis/binding assay.
unrecoverable_material_gaps.impact: Nonblocking when recorded as a mechanism limitation; direct mechanism claims remain restricted to membrane-integrity, permeability, and microscopy evidence.
